entries.title: Vendor / Operator Identity (whisper.identify)
entries.purpose: Name the vendor and operator role behind a host or IP in one call.

exec.cypher: CALL whisper.identify([$v]) YIELD host, vendor_id, canonical_name, category, roles, host_class, band

exec.cypher: CALL whisper.assess([$v]) YIELD host, label, band, sub_labels, coverage, evidence

entries.prompt: Assess the threat posture of 8.8.8.8. CALL whisper.assess([$v]). Read the label + band + coverage together; coverage:known-clean/benign-allowlisted is a vouch, malicious-evidenced/CRITICAL is a listing. no-data != safe.

exec.cypher: CALL whisper.variants($v) YIELD variant, method, exists, confidence

entries.prompt: Enumerate look-alike variants of paypal.com. CALL whisper.variants($v) (scalar string arg). exists:true means it is registered - triage those first by confidence and method.

exec.cypher: CALL whisper.walk($v) YIELD coverage, host, nearest_known_vendors, no_atlas_match, siblings

entries.title: Threat-Feed Explainer (whisper.explain / explain)

exec.cypher: CALL whisper.explain($v) YIELD indicator, score, level, explanation, sources
exec.altForm: CALL explain($v) is the same engine, bare form (no whisper. prefix, no YIELD); it returns the fuller column set: indicator, type, available, cached, found, score, level, explanation, factors, sources, advisory.

entries.prompt: Explain the threat verdict for paypal.com. CALL whisper.explain($v) for indicator/score/level/explanation/sources, or bare CALL explain($v) for the full card (adds type/found/factors/advisory). level:NONE = not listed; the sources[] name each feed.

entries.prompt: Reduce www.foo.co.uk to its registrable apex. CALL whisper.psl.tldPlusOne($v) -> apex (eTLD+1) using the Public Suffix List.

entries.title: Graph Schema Catalog (db.schema)
entries.purpose: List every node and relationship type in the graph with counts and examples.
entries.why: The self-describing schema: node/relationship types with counts, descriptions, examples, source/target labels and query best-practices - the map of what the graph holds.

entries.title: Submit Observation / Feedback (whisper.submit)
entries.purpose: Contribute an indicator observation or feedback back into the graph (requires an API key).
entries.why: The write channel: submit an indicator/feedback with an attributable API key (anonymous submits are refused to preserve K-anonymity). Keyed-only by design.

exec.altForm: kind:'feedback' takes {observation_id?, query?, results?, comment?, severity?, v?} - all optional, a comment-only report is accepted - and returns the 4-column receipt: observation_id, accepted, advisory, v. Batch: UNWIND $records AS rec CALL whisper.submit(rec) dispatches one call per record, each row in its kind's shape.
exec.note: WRITE channel; needs an API key carrying the submit:write scope (anonymous callers get a clear 400: a write channel requires an attributable API key, preserving K-anonymity). Per-kind CLOSED arg schema, live-verified: kind:'indicator' allows {kind, identifier_kind, value, observation_id?, confidence?, first_seen?, provenance?, v?} and requires identifier_kind + value; kind:'feedback' allows {kind, observation_id?, query?, results?, comment?, severity?, v?}. identifier_kind is one of ip, asn, cert_sha256, cert_ja3_hash, cert_ja4_hash, cert_jarm, cidr, whois_pattern (plaintext, normalized server-side) or host_hash_rotating, url_path_hash (submitter-side pre-hashed 64-char SHA-256 hex; a plaintext host/URL is rejected, never auto-hashed). results is a list of strings. An unknown key or kind is rejected with a clear 400 naming the allowed set.

entries.prompt: Submit an observation to the graph. CALL whisper.submit({kind:'indicator', identifier_kind:'ip', value:$v}) with a key carrying submit:write (writes are keyed; anonymous gets a clear 400). identifier_kind: ip / asn / cert_sha256 / cert_ja3_hash / cert_ja4_hash / cert_jarm / cidr / whois_pattern in plaintext, or host_hash_rotating / url_path_hash pre-hashed (64-char SHA-256 hex). kind:'feedback' files a free-form report ({query?, results?, comment?, severity?}). The indicator ack returns observation_id, accepted, idempotent, promotion_state and a bucketed k_bucket (below / promoted), never a raw count.
